facts.fact: Law 2009-010 (art. 2) places civil registration under the joint supervision of the minister for territorial administration and the minister for justice, who organise, run and control it; declarations are received in the communes by mayors or their delegates (art. 5), and communes buy the registers on the ministry's single model (art. 9).

systems.owner: ministry for territorial administration and ministry of justice (joint supervision); kept by mayors and civil-status agents
systems.tiers: a centre d'état civil in every urban commune, rural commune and commune d'arrondissement, with secondary centres where needed; diplomatic and consular posts; centres outside communes continue until communal structures exist

systems.owner: hospitals, maternities and public or private health facilities
systems.tiers: health facilities; consultable by the civil-status officer

note: The law names no software and states no office as registering digitally. Art. 15 says registration and keeping of acts are 'manuels et/ou informatisés' and that computerised acts have the same legal value as manual ones: a permission, not a statement of practice, and no value of 'made' or 'events' fits it. The register it describes is a bound register of five-part leaves (arts. 10-13): part 1 kept at the centre, part 2 sent up to the ministry for national centralisation, part 3 yearly to the court, part 4 monthly to the regional statistics directorate, part 5 to the declarant. Births declared within 45 days (art. 18), deaths within 15 days (art. 23).
